title: Tenant-centric console intake routing and delivery commitment matrix
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: High volume of console/reporting asks from enterprise tenants with mixed business value leads to unpredictable delivery timelines and engineering context-switch cost. Goal: Define a tenant-centric intake router and commitment matrix that maps incoming requests (usage exports, cost breakdowns, dashboard slices) to delivery lanes with explicit SLA/risk/effort commitments and a deterministic owner for acceptance and delivery. This ticket is the PM spec and coordination hub for scoping MVP automation rules and the manual fallback path for edge/strategic customers.
acceptance_criteria: Define 4 delivery lanes (Self-serve, Fast-track enterprise, Scheduled batch, Concierge/Professional Services) with clear eligibility criteria and SLA windows
Document routing rules that map request attributes (tenant size, monthly spend, security tier, export cadence, data retention) to lanes
Produce a commitment matrix that lists expected turnaround, owner role, required artifacts, and cost estimate for each lane
Integrate routing decision into intake form (console + support) with recommended lane output for user and internal assignee
Create a dashboard to surface intake backlog by lane, average lead time, and top blocking factors
Stakeholders (Support, Solutions, Eng, Design) have reviewed and signed off on the routing rules and commitment matrix
notes: Trade-offs: aggressive automation reduces manual triage time but risks misclassifying strategic tenants. MVP will bias toward conservative assignment for tenants with high ARR or regulatory needs.
We will avoid building heavy ML classification for this phase; rules are explicit and parameterized to allow quick iteration.
Retention and PII-sensitive exports will always route to Concierge/Professional Services lane regardless of spend.
Cost-estimate model: provide a rough engineering-hour to calendar-day mapping per lane for SRE and Eng capacity planning.
